title: Group Kit Result Views Into Browsing Sessions
prompt: You are analyzing user engagement on a diagnostic test kit platform. Users log in to view their lab results, and each view is recorded with a timestamp. A browsing session is defined as a sequence of result views where consecutive views are separated by 30 minutes or less. If more than 30 minutes elapse between two views for the same user, a new session begins. Write a query that assigns a unique session identifier to each user's session and calculates the number of result views per session. Output columns: `user_id`, `session_id` (unique within user, starting from 1 for their first session), `view_count`. Order by `user_id` ASC, `session_id` ASC. The schema includes one table tracking every time a user views their test results. Handle users who have only one view in a session (edge case). Test your query by ensuring it correctly groups views separated by gaps greater than 30 minutes into distinct sessions.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE result_views (view_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INT NOT NULL, kit_id VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, viewed_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, result_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL);

composite_moves: CTE1: LAG(viewed_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY viewed_at) to get previous timestamp per user
CTE1: CASE WHEN previous_ts IS NULL OR viewed_at - previous_ts > INTERVAL '30 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as new_session_flag
CTE2: SUM(new_session_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY viewed_at ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as session_id
GROUP BY user_id, session_id to count views per session

hints: Think about how to detect when a new session starts for each user based on the time gap between consecutive views.
Use LAG to find the previous view timestamp for each user, then flag rows where the gap exceeds 30 minutes or there is no previous view.
Assign session identifiers by taking a cumulative sum of the new-session flags within each user's timeline, then group by user and session to count views.
answer_key:
WITH flagged AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    viewed_at,
    LAG(viewed_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY viewed_at) AS previous_ts,
    CASE
      WHEN LAG(viewed_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY viewed_at) IS NULL
           OR viewed_at - LAG(viewed_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY viewed_at) > INTERVAL '30 minutes'
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS new_session_flag
  FROM result_views
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    viewed_at,
    SUM(new_session_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY viewed_at ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_id
  FROM flagged
)
SELECT
  user_id,
  session_id,
  COUNT(*) AS view_count
FROM sessions
GROUP BY user_id, session_id
ORDER BY user_id, session_id;

_meta.scenario: an at-home diagnostic test kit platform tracking kit shipped and results released
